$comment: Input-layer parity matrix (decision 8, AC5). Every capability cell is at parity, an allowlisted gap with an owner and an expiry, or a documented divergence carrying a rationale and no date. The gate (scripts/__tests__/input-parity.node.mjs) enumerates the input surface itself and FAILS on a capability with no cell, a cell with no valid status, a gap with no live allowlist entry, or a divergence with no rationale. An expired allowlist entry fails the gate — that is what makes an expiry real.

cells.claim: single-line text field: states, boundary, height tier, focus
multi-line field: states, boundary, own floor
native select with token chevron; read-only exists in neither content model
on/off control: 24px floor bare, checked serializes, unchecked ABSENT, read-only unsupported in both layers
one-thumb range: keyboard, drag, min/max/step, RTL, serialization

cells.plainCss: RangeBounds recipe — two named .weft-slider in a named fieldset

cells.claim: search pattern: hidden label, leading glyph, named clear appearing only with content
the clear's behaviour: empty the value, keep focus, one change + one commit
one deduplicated commit signal per transaction
the naming ladder: visible label, hidden label, icon-only aria-label
help and error compose to one ordered describedby list, error first
real text plus the native attribute; the name never carries a glyph
a choice group exposes an accessible group name
resting tier 2: underline-only boundary at 3:1, behaviour unchanged
resting tier 3: bordered field, quieter colour
choice row at the 32px row height with the 44px clearance stack
choice row; grouped rows carry a group name

allowlist.capability: commit signal — blur, Enter, explicit save — emitted as one deduplicated transaction
allowlist.reason: A commit boundary is a JavaScript behaviour, and the plain-CSS layer ships no script — a sandboxed panel iframe gets no commit signal from Weft today. Parity would be a dependency-free DOM helper on the raw-color-pattern.js precedent, not a CSS rule; the sequence contract it would implement is already documented in 04-design-system.md.

allowlist.capability: the search clear's behaviour: set empty, dispatch one input event, refocus, commit
allowlist.reason: Three lines of consumer JS documented in the recipe — a stylesheet cannot write a value. The same dependency-free helper that would close the commit-boundary gap closes this one, so the two entries share an owner and an expiry deliberately.

divergences.capability: bounded range — two values, one control
divergences.plainCss: RangeBounds recipe: two named .weft-slider inputs in a named fieldset
divergences.rationale: React's Radix Slider is array-valued and multi-thumb by default; a native input type=range has exactly one thumb and never two without scripting, which the plain-CSS layer exists to avoid. An expiry would imply parity is coming; it is not, deliberately. The recipe is first-class: group name, serialization, keyboard and RTL are all tested, and From-at-or-below-To stays consumer-owned validation under decision 7.

divergences.capability: checkbox-row — the 32px row with the 44px clearance stack
divergences.rationale: The ROW is a plain-CSS recipe: .weft-checkbox-wrap/.weft-radio-wrap carry the 32px row height and the 12px stack gap that puts adjacent rows exactly 44px apart. React ships the bare control and composes rows through Label/FormItem, where the surface owns spacing — a React Row primitive would duplicate a layout the form composition already answers. Deliberate and permanent, like RangeBounds: an expiry would imply a Row component is coming, and it is not. The clearance contract itself is measured on the recipe by input-geometry and input-clearance, and React surfaces inherit it by adopting the stack pattern, which the gallery demonstrates.

divergences.capability: radio-row — the 32px row with the 44px clearance stack
divergences.rationale: The ROW is a plain-CSS recipe: .weft-checkbox-wrap/.weft-radio-wrap carry the 32px row height and the 12px stack gap that puts adjacent rows exactly 44px apart. React ships the bare control and composes rows through Label/FormItem, where the surface owns spacing — a React Row primitive would duplicate a layout the form composition already answers. divergences.capability: select — choosing one option from a list
divergences.rationale: React Select is Radix: a popover listbox with typeahead, portalled content and styled options. The plain-CSS .weft-select is a native <select> whose dropdown belongs to the platform and cannot be styled by design. Same need, permanently different mechanisms — an expiry would imply the native picker will someday grow Radix behaviour. What IS held common and tested: the trigger geometry (tier + sm step through the same tokens), the boundary pair, the chevron invariant across palettes, name/description wiring, and form serialization.
